messages.subject: How to construct two-way mixed ANOVA in procD.lm
parts:
Q1: I would like to construct a two-way mixed ANOVA model to test statistical significance of DA and FA. As far as I know, side should be a fixed factor (DA), ind should be a random factor, and their interaction (FA) should be included as well. Without consideration of replication, I can construct the following formula: fit1 <- procD.lm(shape ~ side * ind). Since ind is a random vector, I am thinking to use anova(fit, error = c(...)) to update the denominator for F-value, but which MS should I choose for side, ind, and side:ind? Or maybe am I completely off the correct direction?

Q2: If I wish to incoporate replication into the model, how should I then update the model (fit2 <- procD.lm(shape ~ side...), anova(fit2, error = c()))?

Q3: If I have repeated quantified shape of the same individual during their growth and development 4 times and would like to compare shape changes over time, is the following model correct? fit3 <- procD.lm(shape ~ ind/time), anova(fit3, error = c("ind:time", "Residual")).

The following tables from "FLUCTUATING ASYMMETRY: Measurement, Analysis, Patterns" seems relevant to the construction of fit1 and fit2, in order:



But I am really curious about how to convert them to code in geomorph. My specimen is of object symmetry. Do I need to create a reflected and relabeled copy of shape and combine them for analysis, as did in bilat.symmetry? I do not even know how to trick bilat.symmetry into doing what I want. Without specifying replication, the ind:side is just the residual relabeled and no F-value would be returned to indicate significance of FA. You help is very much appreciated.


Best regards,

Patrick Lv

Patrick,

data(PlethMorph)
fitGLS <- lm.rrpp(TailLength ~ SVL, data = PlethMorph, Cov = PlethMorph$PhyCov, print.progress = FALSE, iter = 999)

It can be seen that all individuals are given the same covariance matrix, which has 3 rows and 3 columns (rather than 30 rows and 30 columns) that account for correlated error structure for 3 repeated measures over time. In my fit3, if I have 3 repeated measures for each of the 10 individuals, resulting in a total of 30 specimens (the "shape" variable is a 3D list of p*k*30 dimension), what is the appropriate dimension for the covariance matrix if I wish to include cov argument into fit3 to account for correlated error structure? Should it be a 30*30 matrix (since I have 30 specimens in total) or 3*3 matrix (since each ind is measured 3 times)? I would like to construct a matrix of suitable dimension with first order auto-regression and first order moving average error structure.

Patrick, the example of RRPP is one of a phylogenetic GPS, i.e. to account for phylogenetic relatedness among species observations while fitting the model. As such, the expected covariance matrix (reflected in the error term) has dimensions that correspond to those of the observations (species values for TailLength and SVL in that example).

Your case is a bit different, as the structured error would be only with respect to the time observations within individuals, not across them. That is, you still expect the individuals to have independent random errors associated, but you may expect the three observations of each individual to be autocorrelated due to the time dimension of your experiment. So this gets a bit complicated.

I guess that for the model to run you would still need a 30x30 matrix, but that matrix would have to accurately reflect the expected structure for your error, i.e. have the matrix you inferred for the time dependence for the blocks within individuals and a structure with ~N(1, 0) across individuals. 

But to be honest, I´m not completely sure how that might run in RRPP and if it would actually provide the required output. Maybe Mike can help with that if he has the time.

Cheers,

Antigoni

You could attempt to use a Kronecker product to obtain a 30 x 30 matrix that has the 10 3 x 3 identical matrices for individuals.  Using your code, do something like this:

R <- corMatrix(cs2ARMA2)[[1]]

If you have your data arranged as three sets of 10 measurements per individual, then 

Cov <- kronecker(R, diag(10))

If you have your data arranged as 10 sets of three measurements, then

Cov <- kronecker(diag(10), R)

Either way works as long as the structure of Cov match the rows of your data.  Your example data used the former approach.  However, the latter approach shows better how a Kronecker product generalizes the 3 x 3 matrix to a 30 x 30 Covariance matrix for all observations (just easier to see with one’s eye what is going on).

Patrick, the example of RRPP is one of a phylogenetic GPS, i.e. to account for phylogenetic relatedness among species observations while fitting the model. As such, the expected covariance matrix (reflected in the error term) has dimensions that correspond to those of the observations (species values for TailLength and SVL in that example).

Your case is a bit different, as the structured error would be only with respect to the time observations within individuals, not across them. That is, you still expect the individuals to have independent random errors associated, but you may expect the three observations of each individual to be autocorrelated due to the time dimension of your experiment. So this gets a bit complicated. 

I guess that for the model to run you would still need a 30x30 matrix, but that matrix would have to accurately reflect the expected structure for your error, i.e. have the matrix you inferred for the time dependence for the blocks within individuals and a structure with ~N(1, 0) across individuals.
